A1.justification: Both readable PDFs describe the same KinMo framework and HumanML3D experiments. Their equations, figures and tables can be matched reliably. v1 ends with references; v2 includes supplementary Appendices A–G. Assessments concern the content actually supplied in these PDFs.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original retrieval, generation, editing, trajectory-control and ablation results, plus a 20-participant user study.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain original empirical results and report additional generation comparisons, diagnostic analyses and control results for other body parts.

M1.justification: The annotation, HTMA, reasoner, coarse-to-fine generation and trajectory-control pipeline is retained. However, v2 Eq. (3) adds connecting-joint angular velocity to the interaction representation, while Appendix G retains the earlier expression. The PDFs do not resolve whether this changes the implemented representation or corrects its description; expanded architecture details alone do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: The same HumanML3D-derived data and principal tasks remain. v2 adds retrieval between global and low-level descriptions in both directions (Table 7), and trajectory-control evaluations for the torso, arms and legs beyond the retained pelvis experiment (Table 11). These extend scenarios within the existing domain.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds GuidedMotion, KP, FG-MDM, FineMoGen and ParCo, while removing MotionDiffuse and T2M-GPT from that generation comparison. New Table 3 evaluates LGTM- and FineMoGen-based description alternatives and a ParCo-style two-group configuration. This substantially expands comparison with closely related approaches; retrieval, editing and pelvis-control comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The original data split, four retrieval protocols, editing sample count and user-study design remain. Added evaluations introduce a shared MoMask generator while varying descriptions (Table 3), an RQ-base-layer configuration (Table 5), and all-joint training for control (Appendix D.5). Newly disclosed training settings elsewhere do not establish revisions to existing experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled description-source and two-versus-six-group comparisons (Table 3), encoder-by-hierarchy results (Table 5), tri-modal alignment diagnostics (Table 7), and description-order ablations (Table 8). Figure 12 adds a short-transition failure case. These substantially deepen analysis beyond v1's semantic-level ablation and training curves, which are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Section 5.2 newly specifies different random seeds during inference. Both versions already report 20 generation evaluations with 95% confidence intervals, and both describe an annotation-agreement threshold above 0.8. The additional seed disclosure does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: v1's Table 2 Ours row is retained as Ours (CLIP), including FID 0.050 and top-3 R-Precision 0.817. v2 adds an HTMA row reporting 0.039 and 0.821, respectively; this is an additional configuration, not a demonstrated same-configuration improvement. New comparator, ablation, tri-modal retrieval and all-joint-control results substantially expand the evidence. Original retrieval, editing and pelvis-control values are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix G adds formal motion-state definitions, Proposition 1 and a reconstruction proof under a rigid-body assumption, including position, rotation and velocity derivations in Eqs. (12)–(19). v1 only asserts reversibility and refers to supplementary material absent from its supplied PDF. The main interaction-velocity definition also changes.

C1.justification: Both abstracts, contribution lists and conclusions retain the same central contributions: a three-level kinematic representation and annotation pipeline, hierarchical text-motion alignment, and coarse-to-fine synthesis supporting editing and control. v2 emphasizes linguistic describability and modality ambiguity more explicitly, without materially changing these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies motion-understanding evidence as retrieval in the Section 4 footnote, interprets asymmetric global/low-level text retrieval in Appendix D.1, and identifies poor descriptions and missed short transitions as failure conditions in Appendix F. Appendix G limits reconstruction to rigid-group motion and motivates temporal approximation. These add substantial explanations and applicability boundaries. Section 5.3's claim of superior CLIP alignment nevertheless conflicts with Table 5's reported metrics.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C supply annotation prompts and examples, the 0.8 keyframe threshold, annotation effort and cost, 70-epoch HTMA training, network dimensions, codebook settings, optimizer and learning-rate schedule, batch sizes, guidance scales and spatial-encoder details. v1 largely defers these details to an unavailable supplement. These are substantial documentation additions, without establishing that retained experiments changed settings.

R1.justification: Section 2 now positions KinMo explicitly against LGTM, FG-MDM, FineMoGen and ParCo, distinguishing its kinematic descriptions from existing additional-caption and body-decomposition approaches. Related citations and broader multimodal context expand substantially, while the earlier ChatPose and PoseFix discussion disappears. This revises the substantive comparison context.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution descriptions and method exposition undergo extensive rewriting around describable representations and modality ambiguity. v2 creates a separate motion-understanding-and-generation section, reorganizes experiments, and moves detailed editing, control and training-curve discussion into appendices. This is substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 substantially redraws and reorganizes the pipeline diagrams into Figures 2–3, including an explicit retrieval diagram. Editing and pelvis-control tables move from Tables 3–4 to Appendix Tables 9–10, and training curves move to Figure 10. New comparison tables, annotation illustrations, control examples, a study-interface screenshot and a failure visualization substantially expand the displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves reproducibility and empirical scrutiny: Appendices B–C provide details that v1 only refers to, while closer baselines and controlled description, decomposition and ordering comparisons better test the central rationale. Failure analysis and explicit reconstruction assumptions also improve assessment of applicability. Inconsistent velocity definitions and the erroneous interpretation accompanying Table 5 remain, but the gains in documentation and diagnostic evidence provide a substantial net quality improvement.
